## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Anuruddhattheraapadāna* is a biographical and karmic poem in the *Therāpadāna* collection of the Pali Khuddakanikāya [SuttaCentral]. It recounts the past deeds and spiritual attainments of the elder Anuruddha (*Anuruddhatthera*). The SuttaCentral database records five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].
Computational text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus reveals substantial internal alignment with Pali commentarial and canonical literature. Extensive portions of the poem are shared with both parts of the commentary on the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Dutiyo bhāgo and Paṭhamo bhāgo), including an extensive match of verses §1.1–13.1 [DharmaNexus]. In addition, segment §13.1–14.1 shares text reuse with the *Tuvaradāyakattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 243) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also aligns several segments with non-Pali Buddhist literature, finding moderate cross-language matches with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* (especially §9.1–9.3 and §11.4), alongside lower-scoring alignments with the Sanskrit *Gaṇḍavyūhasūtra* and the Tibetan *Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra* (D0119) [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
